title: So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE)
summary: A three-hour live stream where NH reviews about 15 viewer programs one after another, between chat questions on training, diet, cardio and his own lifting. The same corrections keep coming up: too little or badly spread back volume, rep ranges that are too wide or too high, redundant exercises, badly ordered supersets, and bodyweight pull-ups that should be weighted.
claims: The number one requirement for progress in any part of fitness is the ability to be intense and push yourself; people without it stay small whatever program they run, while intense people gain even with no program
He trained a strongman friend who went to failure even on a warm-up set; on his first try at dumbbell pullovers he went 40, 55, 65 and ended doing 70 lb for sets of 10 while NH used 100 lb
Without weights, ring rows done with the feet walked far back, so the pull turns into an upright row, are a good substitute
He dislikes the Arnold split: too many exercises per muscle in one session is junk volume for a natural; for chest, one horizontal press, one incline and one isolation is plenty
To run push/pull/legs on 4-5 days instead of 6, simply cut one of the days
Shortened-biased movements are one option for the brachialis, but he prefers to train it through full range of motion
He still agrees with 99% of his hypertrophy series; it is the basis of his bodybuilding methodology
Face pulls done seated in the lat pulldown machine are good; people do them standing only because the person who popularized them did

Rep range depends on the intensity technique: rest-pause or drop sets need higher reps; after a 10-rep set to failure, resting 15-20 s gives about 5 more reps, 50% extra volume; without such a reason he stays in lower rep ranges
Keep your phone out of training: put music on shuffle and do not touch it; people scrolling between sets rush their work and then wonder why they do not grow
He currently maintains, eating mostly carbs, and plans to start bulking again soon
He has no interest in an extreme cut; he carries a lot of fat and will cut in a year or two, but cutting mostly matters for competitors or photos
He was stuck about two years in intermediate hell during his powerbuilding phase; novices can do anything, but intermediates must program precisely
Many fitness YouTubers, Jeff Nippard included, bulk too aggressively and carry lots of fat; he sees no point and it hurts his mental health
His favourite shoulder lifts now: Smith overhead press (grindable, rest-pause friendly), standing single-arm military press with a slow negative, cuffed lateral raise once a week, and dips
He is working towards weighted dips with four plates for 4x5, but gym plates are so big his legs already spread wide
At 6 ft he can no longer get a full lat stretch on his gym's pulldown because the stack bottoms out; he needed a gym pin to go above 200 lb
A natural can only get unhealthily big by getting fat; lean he would be about 190-195 lb, and 220 lb lean is not possible for him
Tuna is fine for mercury if eaten about twice a week in small amounts
Weighted pull-ups work in 3-5, 4-8 or 5-8; 6-10 is getting high; weighted chin-ups are best kept around 6-10 to protect the biceps
An upper day of bench, weighted pull-ups, DB overhead press, cable curls, pushdowns and reverse pec deck is cookie-cutter but effective; it lacks triceps long head, abs and forearm work
Keep bench and pull-ups as standalone lifts for focus, then superset DB overhead press with curls and pushdowns with reverse pec deck; the day drops to about 1h10 and leaves room for forearms and abs
Starting both upper days with a chest press means chest is the priority; never start a day with your heavy shoulder press if chest comes first
He is not a fan of the seated cable row; a dumbbell row or a pullover is a better choice
On EZ-bar skull crushers do not ego lift with plates you have not earned
Two upper days should be 72-90 hours apart, within two or three days of each other; more rest is not needed
Hack squat at 6-10 reps is low; it can go into the 10-15 range
After hack squat and Smith split squat the quads are done; adding leg extensions is junk volume
The posterior chain can take more volume than the quads
Weighted sit-ups should be done on a shallow decline of about 10-15 and must be intense
RDL at 8-10 is an odd range that makes progression hard; use 6-10
Smith squat plus leg press on the same day is redundant; pick one
Knee raises are a highly recommended ab exercise because they stretch the spine and make it feel better
Three sets of pull-ups and three sets of rows a week builds a weak back; fix it with lat work on upper days and trap work (Kroc rows, power shrugs) on lower days
Add a neck exercise on each lower day
Upper/lower is a split built for accumulating a lot of volume, so minimal upper/lower days waste it
He trains neck flexion and extension but never side flexion because he dislikes the feeling; rotation work matters for drivers or combat athletes, not bodybuilders
Novices get tremendous results training 2-3 days a week for about an hour; enjoy it because later you will be forced to train 4-5 times
Neck training does not cause sleep apnea: at 240 lb with a smaller neck he had bad apnea, at 220 lb with a bigger neck he has none
Do three sets per exercise as a novice or intermediate, two as an advanced lifter; a fourth set is icing, only if you still have juice and it feels good
Rotating bench press and Smith bench week to week allows constant progression with fewer injuries; use the same rep range
He has replaced leg raises in his programs with knee raises loaded with a dumbbell between the feet
Supersetting hack squat with abs works because it recruits the core less than barbell squats; training abs every session is fine if kept to 2-3 sets
The dip rep range should always be lower than the ring push-up rep range
An arm day should add volume that already exists on other days, not be the only place arms get trained, and it can still include compounds
From 50+ physique reviews most viewers are back dominant, yet the programs sent to him lack back work
Train back at least three times a week, frequently and hard with a lot of volume; never put all back volume on one back day
Kroc rows are incredibly underrated: unmatched for traps and upper back and very safe; back can be pushed hard with little injury risk
For a dips plus dumbbell row superset take about a minute between the two and 3-4 minutes between rounds so both stay intense
If weighted dips make you anxious, pause them and use a higher rep range
Behind-the-neck press is great if you have the mobility; always ramp up to it light first
On cable crunches control the negative; moving the whole stack for five trembling reps does little
Reverse wrist curls work best around 15-20 reps
The deadlift-style barbell row (reset at the floor, torso fairly upright) is not his favourite but has value for the posterior chain and upper back; control the negative and prefer 8-12
Bulgarian split squat at 6-10 is low; try 10-15
Forearms recover fast enough to isolate on consecutive days with different curl types
Upright rows belong in a 10-15 rep range
Once you can do 10 clean bodyweight pull-ups or chin-ups, add weight and use 4-8 or 6-10; bodyweight reps no longer grow an intermediate
Bulgarian split squats in a giant set are close to suicidal; after his split squats he just sits for three minutes
To break a weighted pull-up plateau add lat pulldown variations and back-off sets: max reps at the top weight, then remove 5-10 lb
Back can be trained every day on upper/lower because it is many muscles; train different aspects each day
Bulking is not required for novices or intermediates to gain; it only makes progression easier
Do cardio after lifting, on another day, or at another time of day, never before training, because it should be intense and would hurt performance
His rep ranges run from 3 to 20 but most sets are 6-12
A wrestler training 2-3 times a week can cut a novice program to two lifting days with less volume
His cardio is 10 hard minutes after the gym: a run at 7-8 min/mile or the stairmaster with an 80 lb backpack, plus daily walks, swimming or hikes
He supersets freely because he trains at empty hours, and if someone takes a machine he waits or asks to work in
At 22% body fat you cannot judge weak points: neck and forearms look big because they store fat, and upper chest may not really be weak
Never open a day with an isolation movement, and never put two lat movements back to back
Weighted decline sit-ups at 15-20 reps are too high; use 6-10 or 8-12
Do not repeat the exact same lateral raise twice a week; use a different variation
Trap bar shrugs are an underrated movement, good for rugby
A rugby player should keep lower-body compound volume low because the sport already supplies leg work, and use compounds rather than isolation for the upper body
Isolation is the icing on the cake: it complements compounds and must never replace them
Double progression: stay in the range until the first set clears the top, e.g. 8-7-7-5 then 9-8-7-6 then 10 on a 5-10 range, then add about 5 lb to dumbbells
Pullovers belong at 6-10 reps for experienced lifters and 8-12 for novices; 12-20 is too high
Rep ranges whose top is more than double the bottom (8-18, 8-16) are unjustified, nearly impossible to clear and create plateaus; use something like 10-15
Low-bar squat is hard to justify for a bodybuilder unless no hack squat or high-bar squat is possible; low-bar squat plus RDL loads the lower back heavily
Stay in a given rep range for at least a month
Pendlay rows are not a good hypertrophy movement; dumbbell rows are better for lats
Training lower body once a week is fine if you are correcting an upper-body weakness
Three sets of squats and three of front squats is already six heavy quad sets; stop there
To rehab lower-back fatigue use hyperextensions rather than good mornings
Two ab isolations in the same session are redundant
Ending a lower day with a dead hang is a good way to unload a spine that took a lot of loading
Kroc rows at 5-8 encourage too much cheating; 6-10 minimum, prefer 10-15; cheat only in response to fatigue you planned for, never from rep one or out of ego
A very steep incline bench trains shoulders, not upper chest
Smith JM press at 5-8 is asking for injury; go higher
Drop AMRAP sets from bodybuilding programs
Weighted ring push-ups (backpack) are an insanely good chest builder, recommended even by Louie Simmons
Do not superset two energy-expensive compounds such as RDL with chin-ups; give them their own space
Hip thrusts are redundant after squats, RDLs and leg press; he dropped them long ago and finds them weak even for glutes
A muscle that needs catching up rarely needs that much volume; a 6-day schedule like this should drop to four days
Everyone should learn to write their own programs and then have an experienced coach review them
Abs and back can be trained high frequency or high volume, not both; every day means every training day of the split
Forearms need work capacity built gradually or they stay sore for days; he now trains them 3-4 times a week with modest volume
Plateaus come from diet, poor recovery or the program
Never drop to lower reps just to move more weight; a 3RM and 10RM give the same hypertrophic stimulus, so pick the one you can progress on without getting hurt
High-bar squat at 10-15 is very cardio-taxing; use 6-10
Save time by doing your first working set of reverse curls right after the last squat warm-up
Narrow-handle seated rows are unproductive; use a wide grip for traps, and vertical pulls for lats
The higher the rep range, the harder it is to clear it and add weight
Full body three times a week works best Monday-Wednesday-Friday, giving 48 h between sessions and a full weekend after peak fatigue
A Bulgarian split squat should never close a superset, and never superset two lower-body compounds
For joint-friendly training choose cable curls over preacher curls and cable triceps extensions over overhead or dumbbell ones
Recovery is the number one reason people have joint issues
For a V-taper add upright rows and weighted pull-ups
For glutes, do split squats rather than hip thrusts
On upright rows ignore form advice and try cable, dumbbell and barbell; he only likes dumbbells
One set per exercise at 4-8 reps, HIT style, is nonsense; frequency exists to fit volume in, not the reverse
One set of biceps a day even seven days a week is only 7 sets; intensity does not compensate because a normal lifter's first set is just as intense
Old-school routines like Arnold's six-day body-part splits are poor programming for naturals
A deload of two sets at 2 RIR is a reasonable deload
Do not skip the bottom of calf raises; that range is where most of the growth comes from
On five days a week cut volume 15-20% versus a four-day plan
Biceps on upper days and triceps on the following lower day ruins triceps performance, since upper days already hit triceps
A static rep target like 3x6 is poor for hypertrophy; use a range like 6-10
Neck at 10-30 reps is too wide; keep it high-rep for safety but 10-20
Twelve back sets in one day after deadlifts is wasted; split back volume across the week
The deadlift is an energy vampire; RDLs or stiff-leg deadlifts plus spinal erector isolation give better hypertrophy at less fatigue and risk
Kroc rows do not train side delts; for side delts he favours lateral raises over upright rows, which are more of a general yoke builder
He prefers some arm work on torso days and compounds on arm days; an isolation-only arm day can serve as an active rest day
A loaded back extension can be the main posterior-chain builder for legs, glutes and back
Balance quad and posterior-chain work in each lower day rather than 70/30 biased days
Light dumbbell pullovers get the shoulders used to the range; once you can go heavy consistently, drop the light day
For finger curls on a cable station he likes the metal handle attachments
A tall lifter struggling to gain should prioritise eating more and patience, since long limbs take a long time to fill out
Large rep drop-off between sets shows low work capacity, mostly trainable, partly genetic
Doing pull-ups unweighted for elbow pain is only temporary; change grip, use fat grips or neutral grip
His commercial-gym days are about 24 sets total in under two hours; around 30-34 sets per day is a heavy day
On four-day upper/lower do 18-24 sets per upper day and 16-20 per lower day
On four days a week do around 20 sets per session; on five days around 14-15
If storms keep you from the gym, build a cheap home gym with a pull-up bar for weighted calisthenics
Two arm days a week is hard to justify; usually one, at most two
exercises: lat builder he prefers over cable pullover
Seated face pull in lat pulldown machine
pause if anxious; lower reps than ring push-ups
lat mass; plateau fix via pulldowns and back-off sets
underrated, safe trap and upper back builder
not good for hypertrophy; use dumbbell row
main posterior chain builder; low back rehab
taxing on elbow with full ROM; cable curl friendlier
core recruited less, superset with abs

says it is weak for his bodyweight

biceps on upper and triceps on lower
pain under chest on dumbbell row
